subject: Request: Enable 'safety-latch' auto-failover for AcmePay A/B test
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Clarke <timothy@acmepay.com>, Sally Green <sally.ops@acmepay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Enable 'safety-latch' auto-failover for AcmePay A/B test

Hi Tim / Sally —

Quick background: AcmePay's engineering team will run an A/B experiment of our v2 model on 10% of production traffic tomorrow (04/02) 10:00–14:00 PT. They requested a lower-latency SLA carveout to evaluate quality tradeoffs. Before we enable the variant route in production, they asked us to enable an automatic mitigation that will (1) pin traffic to the stable model variant (auto-pin) and (2) flip all experiment traffic off if latency or error signals breach safety thresholds — we call this the "safety-latch".

Ask: I need internal approval to enable the safety-latch auto-failover and a temporary SLA exception for the duration of the experiment (4 hours). Our proposal:
- Trigger conditions (any of the following sustained for 5 continuous minutes): p95 latency > 450ms, 5xx rate > 2% of requests, or model token-generation stalls (KV cache miss alarms).
- Action: Immediate pin to stable model + route 100% of AcmePay traffic to stable until manual review; send automated alert and open a ticket to INF-4732.
- Rollback visibility: We will keep a time-limited audit trail and a runbook in Drive.

Attachments: safety-latch-runbook.pdf (playbook + rollback steps), telemetry-thresholds.csv (detailed thresholds by endpoint).

Tim, can you confirm AcmePay ops is comfortable with an automatic pin rather than a manual rollback? Laura / Aditya / Dylan — can you confirm this matches our internal safety requirements, and flag anything that requires legal/finance sign-off (credits/penalties)?

Thanks — short turnaround on this one.

--
Aisha Rahman
Sr. Account Lead, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Timothy Clarke <timothy@acmepay.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Sally Green <sally.ops@acmepay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Enable 'safety-latch' auto-failover for AcmePay A/B test

Thanks Aisha — we prefer an automatic pin for speed. Manual rollback is too slow for the payment flow. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- If the safety-latch pins to stable automatically, will we see the same request IDs and tracing such that our fraud/ops can correlate?
- Can the auto-failover include a percentage ramp-down (e.g., 100% pin after 5 mins, but 50% after 1 minute) so we don't create immediate capacity pressure?

Sally — ops is ok with the thresholds you propose, but we'd like a five-minute cooling window where both systems can elect to hold before a global pin. If you want, we can accept the auto-pin immediately as long as Redwood guarantees an immediate notification and a post-action incident report within 30 minutes.

On Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 09:12 Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick background: AcmePay's engineering team will run an A/B experiment...

Best,
Tim
Timothy Clarke
Head of Production — AcmePay
timothy@acmepay.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Timothy Clarke <timothy@acmepay.com>, Sally Green <sally.ops@acmepay.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Enable 'safety-latch' auto-failover for AcmePay A/B test

Aisha / team —

High-level thumbs up from Runtime. A few operational notes we need to make explicit before greenlight:
1) Capacity shock: we will *not* attempt a partial ramp-down (50% for 1 minute) automatically. Auto-pin must be to stable (100%) to simplify routing and avoid split-KV cache inconsistency. If AcmePay prefers staged ramp-down, that must be a manual play executed by Redwood ops.
2) Telemetry: the thresholds look fine. We'll implement a 5-minute sustained window and require two independent signals (latency + 5xx OR latency + KV stall) before auto-pin, to reduce noisy triggers.
3) Audit & tracing: requests will preserve trace IDs; we'll publish a correlation mapping for AcmePay's side.
4) SLA exception: legal flagged that a temporary SLA deviation requires acceptance of a short-term credits cap in case of breach. Finance/legal want the cap included in HubSpot.

I've attached the Runbook link and telemetry csv for your engineers. If AcmePay accepts the requirement that auto-pin is 100% immediate (no stagger), we can flip the safety-latch to ON for the window requested.

On Thu, Apr 1, 2027 at 10:01 Timothy Clarke <timothy@acmepay.com> wrote:
> Thanks Aisha — we prefer an automatic pin for speed...

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Timothy Clarke <timothy@acmepay.com>, Sally Green <sally.ops@acmepay.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Enable 'safety-latch' auto-failover for AcmePay A/B test

Team —

Approved with conditions:
- We will enable the safety-latch auto-failover for the 04/02 10:00–14:00 PT window provided AcmePay signs the temporary SLA carveout (HubSpot HS-8897). Legal requires the credits cap language be agreed prior to the test.
- Operational rule: auto-pin will be 100% immediate. Aditya's recommendation to require two independent signals before trigger stands. No staged automatic partial ramp-down.
- Notification & reporting: Redwood will send an automated alert to AcmePay Slack and open JIRA INF-4732; incident report to be delivered within 30 minutes of any auto-pin event.
- Post-mortem: if an auto-pin occurs, we will require a joint post-mortem within 3 business days and a mitigations plan for future runs.

@Aisha — please coordinate HubSpot acceptance and have AcmePay sign the SLA carveout doc. @Dylan — prepare a one-page runbook summary for AcmePay ops that lists who to call and the exact telemetry channels.

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
